_README: Hand-curated name -> resource id pins, read by tools/pipeline/validate.py.
THIS IS THE THIRD PLACE A CORRECTION CAN LIVE, and it exists because two
are not enough. build/authored/*.json holds a NAME and never an id -- that
is deliberate, it is what stops a reading pass inventing a number -- so a
name that resolves to the WRONG id cannot be corrected there at all. The
reading is already right. It is the resolver that is wrong.
reading wrong  -> correct build/authored/*.json  (tools/questgraph)
wiki wrong     -> correct build/authored/*.json, basis 'game'
resolver wrong -> HERE
This file is applied INSIDE validate.py, which means it is upstream of all
five hard gates. A pin cannot smuggle a duplicate-evidence row or an
ambiguous zone-less NPC past them. An override layer applied after the
build could, which is why there is not one.
RULES
* Exact names only. No patterns, no substrings, no case folding beyond
what normalize.lua already does. A pin that matched by pattern would be
the bulk text-matching this whole dataset was built to avoid.
* Every pin carries `why`, and `why` must say how the id was DERIVED --
not that it looked right. A wrong pin is a silently wrong marker, which
is worse than the unresolved name it replaces.
* The count is printed at build time. If it moves without somebody
editing this file, something is wrong.
Empty by default, deliberately: with no pins the build is byte-identical to
one that never read this file.
A WORKED EXAMPLE, ready to use but NOT enabled -- see `_candidates`.
PROGRESS.md session 26 records Lexeme Blade I/II/III as 'determinable but
unpinned': all three are literally named 'Lexeme Blade' in res, and they
are separated by damage 226/228/231 ascending with id 20750/20751/20752.
That mapping is derivable from res itself rather than guessed, which is the
standard a pin has to meet. It is left disabled because it has not been
confirmed in game, and this file's whole purpose is to be the place where
a confirmed fact goes.
